title: worker with `type=module` in `use client` page causing error `Uncaught ReferenceError: window is not defined` since 14.0.5-canary.20

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue was opened via the bug report template.

body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://codesandbox.io/p/github/rbox-risk/workerv1_1/main?file=%2Fpackage.json

### To Reproduce

I'm using tensorflow in the worker, so kept this in, otherwise a minimal example with next 14.0.4 (working)
`https://codesandbox.io/p/github/rbox-risk/workerv2_1/main`

In sandbox, client page rendered, `useEffect` loads worker  with `type: module` and worker posts a result back `tf ok` is all went well. 

Confirm error emits with latest release `14.1` and latest canary. 
Error appeared at `canary.20` and confirmed works with `canary.19`.

`https://codesandbox.io/p/github/rbox-risk/workerv1_1/main?file=%2Fpackage.json`

Here worker doesn't return. Hangs on `working...`. In `console` error appears. 

![Capture-worker1](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/assets/59801351/fe4d4829-4dfa-4f8c-8847-4f8174acd27b)



### Current vs. Expected behavior

Expect worker to load, work and return value as per pre `canary.20`

### Provide environment information

```bash
//sandbox instance....

  Platform: linux
  Arch: x64
```

### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Not sure

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

next dev (local), Vercel (Deployed)

### Additional context

Tested on chrome, sandbox, dev local and when deployed to Vercel. Issues remain the same
